subject.title: feat(apps,ui): question surface parity and composer takeover

question: Should OpenClaw make persistent terminal question summaries and web composer takeover the supported cross-platform interaction contract, including the two new shared transport operations?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes interaction and public shared-transport behavior across four clients; green focused tests do not determine whether that permanent product and compatibility contract is desired.

options.title: Sponsor the parity contract
options.body: Approve persistent summaries, Skip, web composer takeover, and the shared transport additions after a current-main merge refresh and native real-behavior proof.

options.title: Narrow the change
options.body: Keep the demonstrated web interaction but split or redesign the shared native transport and parity changes before merge.

options.title: Pause for product design
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers define the long-term cross-surface question interaction and external transport contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the parity contract
recommendation.body: Approve persistent summaries, Skip, web composer takeover, and the shared transport additions after a current-main merge refresh and native real-behavior proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied history shows sustained authorship of the affected cross-platform question-flow work and its follow-up fixes.
